status_note: confirmed on 2.0.0 (Python, macOS arm64) by the probe observations exec-case-when-folded, exec-case-when-folded-empty and exec-case-when-folded-cast
summary: A `CASE` whose later `WHEN` is a constant expression that raises fails while planning, even when no row reaches that `WHEN`: on a table where every row takes the first branch, and on an empty table. The optimizer's `CASE` simplification evaluates every foldable `WHEN` with `ExpressionExecutor::EvaluateScalar`, which throws, where constant folding uses `TryEvaluateScalar` and leaves a failing expression to run time.
At run time `CASE` is lazy (a raising `ELSE` on rows that never reach it does not raise), so the plan-time fold is the one place where a `CASE` branch is evaluated eagerly.
repro: `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 1 x; SELECT CASE WHEN x > 0 THEN 1 WHEN 1 // 0 = 1 THEN 2 END FROM t;` raises `Invalid Input Error: Division by zero in expression (1 // 0)`. The same over `CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER)` (no rows), and `EXPLAIN` of it, raise too; `WHEN 'a'::INTEGER = 1` raises `Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'a' to INT32`.
For contrast, `SELECT CASE WHEN x > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 1 // 0 END FROM t` returns 1.
handling: No workaround yet: duckdb-exec-short-circuit records it for the evaluation-order analysis (#604). The fix upstream would be `TryEvaluateScalar` in `CaseSimplificationRule::Apply`, keeping the `WHEN` when folding fails (https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v2.0.0/src/optimizer/rule/case_simplification.cpp#L15-L46).
